12.head: 717eb58ec018a4c6f09a07e9d52e8920706d618b
12.feedback: {"head":"717eb58ec018a4c6f09a07e9d52e8920706d618b","verdict":"pass","summary":"The change adds a Node-only, read-only reporter (scripts/factory/diagnostics.cjs) invoked only on a failed Claude model step, which builds a bounded, allowlist-only JSON report (fixed tool names, fixed command categories/forms, counts, stop reason) from the pinned action's temporary execution file and uploads it under a separate \"diagnostic-<phase>-<grantId>\" artifact name with 7-day retention. Verified against the current source: the reporter is copied into $RUNNER_TEMP/factory-control before the untrusted ticket head is checked out (same trust boundary already used for worker.cjs), so it cannot be tampered with by ticket/repo content. It correctly distinguishes \"denials array present but empty\" (status=available, denialCount=0) from \"denials missing/invalid\" (status=unavailable, denialCount=null, explicit reason) — never fabricating a zero. File reads are bounded (8 MiB, re-checked after fstat to avoid TOCTOU growth), symlinks/directories are rejected via lstat+O_NOFOLLOW, and the output file is written with O_EXCL so a pre-existing file is refused rather than overwritten. Only three fixed-shape fields (tool, commandCategory, commandForm) ever leave the reporter per denial; raw commands/paths/prompts/IDs/errors are never included, verified by tests that smuggle a synthetic secret through every untrusted field and assert it never appears in the report, stdout, or stderr. The new workflow steps use `continue-on-error: true` and `if: failure() && steps.model.outcome == 'failure'`, so they only fire on an actual model-step failure, can't themselves flip the job back to success, and are skipped for preflight failures or cancellations — confirmed against factory-cycle.yml/factory-pr-review.yml, which gate on job `.result` unaffected by this addition. No other file (policy.cjs, worker.cjs, controller.cjs, permissions blocks, FACTORY_ENABLED gate, turn-ceiling logic) was touched. The new test file is automatically picked up by the existing `yarn test:factory` glob already run in CI, so no CI wiring changes were needed. Regression coverage is strong: missing/oversized/malformed/symlinked/directory inputs, truncation at 100 denials, PowerShell command classification, exact-vs-with-arguments vs compound/dynamic command forms, and non-overwrite of an existing output file are all exercised.","findings":[]}

28.head: 91407deb97d7432c5c786d55ba6a555a46106745
28.feedback: {"head":"91407deb97d7432c5c786d55ba6a555a46106745","verdict":"pass","summary":"This ticket is a follow-up review of PR #27's automatic pickup/merge implementation after a prior independent review (feedback on head d38633d) requested one fix: AutomaticMerger.merge() threw (\"No genuine independent review covers this PR commit\") and failed the `merge` job with a red X whenever it ran against a just-admitted ticket that had not yet reached status \"reviewed\" in the same run (the common case). The new commit (91407de, \"Skip automatic merge cleanly until a ticket is reviewed\") addresses this directly in scripts/factory/merge.cjs: merge() now reads the candidate ticket after authorize()+automaticTicket() provenance checks and, if status !== \"reviewed\" && merge === undefined, returns a clean {merged:false, reason:...} without touching the ledger or calling any GitHub API, instead of falling through to stateTicket()'s reviewGate() throw. I verified: (1) the quick-return runs after automaticTicket() provenance validation, so absent/foreign automatic provenance is still rejected even for unreviewed tickets (scripts/tests/factory-merge.test.cjs \"the unreviewed no-op still refuses absent or foreign automatic provenance\"); (2) the fix does not create a way to silently swallow an inconsistent/dangerous state — if a ticket somehow has merge already defined while status isn't \"reviewed\" (e.g. an in-flight intent), the no-op condition correctly does not trigger and the original throwing path is preserved, with an explicit regression test (\"an unreviewed ticket with merge intent is refused instead of hiding an uncertain merge\"); (3) new parametrized tests cover coding/blocked(with & without PR)/retry/awaiting_review/reviewing statuses, confirming no ledger mutation and no outbound PR/Actions API calls occur; (4) automation.cjs's main() will now complete and exit 0 for this common case since merge() no longer throws, closing the misleading-CI-failure gap described in the feedback. I also re-examined the surrounding authorization/credential-isolation code (policy.cjs authorize/isAutomaticContext/reviewGate/validateState, controller.cjs admit/assess/gate, the factory-app-token action's pinned create-github-app-token SHA, repo-scoped least-privilege permissions, slug validation, and token revocation, and factory-automatic.yml's job conditions) and found it consistent with the ticket's criteria and with the prior reviewer's favorable findings there. No new critical or important issues were found; the single previously identified gap is correctly and narrowly fixed with matching regression coverage.","findings":[]}

29.head: a690f156f94944aee4c4224583b21c4e41135a36
29.feedback: {"head":"a690f156f94944aee4c4224583b21c4e41135a36","verdict":"pass","summary":"The fix correctly removes an accidental double-backslash escaping bug in phoneRegExp: the old literal had `\\\\+`/`\\\\(`/`\\\\)` (matching a literal backslash followed by a quantifier/paren) instead of the intended `\\+`/`\\(`/`\\)` escapes, which is why \"+1 615-555-1212\" and \"(615) 555-1212\" were rejected while a backslash-prefixed number was wrongly accepted. The new regex correctly accepts all four required formats (digits-only, hyphenated, +country-code, and parenthesized area code) and rejects backslash-prefixed, letter-only, and empty input, verified by manual regex-decomposition tracing. \"615-555-\" is correctly rejected because the trailing tail `[0-9]{3,4}?[ -]*[0-9]{3,4}?$` has no provision for a dangling separator before `$`, which also matches the pre-existing Cypress e2e assertion at cypress/tests/ui/user-settings.spec.ts:60-64 that already expects this exact case to fail — so no regression there. The added UserSettingsForm.test.tsx renders the real component and exercises the actual Yup validation schema (no regex duplication), covers accept/reject cases plus a submission test verifying updateUser is called with the typed phone number, and relies only on already-present devDependencies (vitest, @testing-library/react, jest-dom) and the existing vite.config.ts jsdom test setup — no new dependencies. The User fixture in the test matches the User interface exactly, so yarn types should be unaffected. Diff is scoped solely to the regex and new regression tests, consistent with the ticket's scope restrictions.","findings":[]}
